items.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
items.description: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed.

items.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
items.description: WorldBridge generates coherent and controllable 3D worlds from scattered, low-overlap images by encoding references into a global scene context and using attention and latent-reference consistency optimization.

items.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
items.description: Model-driven context management through a context API improves accuracy and token efficiency over harness-triggered compaction, while reusing KV caches after edits reduces prefill compute.

items.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
items.description: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale.

items.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
items.description: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English.

items.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift
items.description: Reasoning-based candidate selection in small language models for entity disambiguation yields negligible in-domain gains but becomes decisive under true zero-shot domain shift, with reranker uncertainty and shift explaining when the paradigms disagree.

items.title: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models

items.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.description: A systematic study of harness design for long-horizon self-evolving autoresearch agents finds that context folding and selective skill deletion improve performance, enabling MLEvolver to achieve strong results on MLE-Bench Lite and KernelBench Level 3.

items.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
items.description: A benchmark and gated decision model enable large language model agents to anticipate user edit requests, improving the precision of shown recommendations.

items.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.description: ELITE enables coding agents to self-improve by integrating complementary implementation mechanisms from independently generated improvements without using downstream task evaluations in the evolution loop, achieving strong SWE-bench performance and transfer.

items.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
items.description: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult.
items.ai_summary: AnyCam uses an anchor object to represent cameras for video generation, enabling scale-aware and view-complete camera control and streaming generation across diverse datasets.

items.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
items.description: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition.
items.ai_summary: AgenTAP is a vision-language model-based agent that autonomously predicts point coordinates and visibility in videos to improve pixel-level localization and track physical points.

items.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
items.description: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver.
items.ai_summary: A low-latency transfer-learning procedure for AI-native autoencoder communications fine-tunes a small subset of layers to adapt to new channel conditions while reducing training time and energy consumption.

items.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
items.description: Image-to-Video Transfer improves pretrained video editors by training them as image editors on single images, enabling new video editing tasks and state-of-the-art results on OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.

items.title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
items.description: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait.
items.ai_summary: LuxAvatar is a feed-forward framework that uses an animatable 3D Gaussian proxy and a neural shader to achieve real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait.

items.title: A Mesh for Every Moment
items.description: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame.
items.ai_summary: MEMO is a dynamic scene reconstruction method that uses a per-Gaussian motion model and track-based initialization to extract accurate meshes at every frame from multi-camera captures.

items.title: Tokenisation is not in APX
items.description: In this paper, we prove that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, meaning that tokenisation is not in the APX complexity class.
items.ai_summary: Research proves that polynomial-time algorithms cannot find an optimal tokenizer within any constant factor unless P equals NP, meaning tokenization is not in the APX complexity class.

items.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
items.description: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together.
items.ai_summary: An empirical study tests whether generated helper images improve visual reasoning and finds that image generation actually lowers mean accuracy across multiple vision-language models.

items.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
items.description: AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment.
items.ai_summary: Research demonstrates that AI monitor evaluation results are highly sensitive to the chosen attack policy and optimization level, which can easily mislead evaluations of monitor strength in deployment.

items.title: DynMF2: Rigid Motion Factorization by Expectation-Maximization for Monocular 4D Reconstruction and Motion Segmentation
items.description: A single casual video leaves a moving scene under-determined: a point seen once from each place can slide toward or away from the camera and still match every frame. We constrain the reconstruction with the structure of the motion itself.
items.ai_summary: DynMF2 is a rigid motion factorization method that uses expectation-maximization on 3D point trajectories to perform monocular 4D reconstruction and motion segmentation without requiring masks.

items.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
items.description: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents.
items.ai_summary: BioScore is an unsupervised benchmark that uses spatial transcriptomics and sparse autoencoders to quantify how well pathology image encoders capture distinct cell identities.

items.title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
items.description: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.description: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling.
items.ai_summary: DART is a trace-mining method that decomposes rejected math reasoning traces and generates distinct alternative candidates to expand problem coverage and improve large language model post-training.

items.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
items.description: A Mixture-of-Loops Transformer reuses key-value memory across loops and depths, and its U-shaped variant improves pretraining efficiency and inference latency.

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.description: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session.
items.ai_summary: Mu-Bench is a benchmark designed to evaluate voice agents on joint task completion, user privacy, and multi-user coordination in closed-loop, full-duplex shared voice interactions.

items.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
items.description: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions.
items.ai_summary: Cairn is a hierarchical planning framework that uses object-centric 3D trajectory priors to steer frozen vision-language-action models around obstacles without requiring fine-tuning.

items.title: LiveVAE: Causal Window Attention Makes Efficient Streaming Video VAE
items.description: While video diffusion models have grown faster and increasingly streamable, the video VAE remains a primary latency bottleneck across interactive generation and editing pipelines.

items.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
items.description: Real-time autoregressive video generators stream minutes of video and accept new prompts on the fly, but struggle to keep people, objects, and places consistent over a long interactive story.

items.title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
items.description: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs.
items.ai_summary: Mathematical analysis derives exact error probabilities and explicit optimal window lengths for sliding-window estimators tracking hidden regime-switching processes under stochastic noise.

items.title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
items.description: Processing long videos with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is prohibitively expensive, making informative frame selection essential for accurate video understanding.
items.ai_summary: ProbFaS is a training- and label-free probabilistic video frame selection pipeline that fuses dense image-text alignment scores with sparse model judgments to improve multimodal large language models' video understanding.

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
items.description: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind.
items.ai_summary: Earth Observation embeddings from the TerraMind foundation model are used to detect, localize, and classify maritime vessels from Sentinel-1 radar imagery while bypassing the original data.

items.title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
items.description: How an object deforms when it hits the ground reveals what it is made of.
items.ai_summary: PhysReader is a sim-to-real feed-forward predictor that estimates deformable object material properties like stiffness and yield stress from single videos and 2D optical-flow tracklets.

items.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
items.description: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one.
items.ai_summary: This review examines the statistical foundations and modern challenges of the look-elsewhere effect in particle physics searches, covering continuous scans, multiple discrete tests, and machine learning interactions.

items.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
items.description: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning.
items.ai_summary: A hybrid decision tree architecture integrates feature-based and selective case-based splits using informative subsets of features to improve predictive accuracy while maintaining interpretability.

items.title: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
items.description: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from…
items.ai_summary: FineDex is a framework that learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions from fine-grained instructions to improve dexterous manipulation success and enable deployment on physical humanoid robots.

items.title: Stranger Things: When Objects Appear Without Their Typical Neighbors
items.description: Visual context is a powerful cue for object recognition: scenes inform what, where, and at what scale objects are likely to appear.
items.ai_summary: STRANGE-Bench is a photorealistic diagnostic benchmark measuring typicality bias in vision models when objects appear outside their usual spatial contexts.

items.title: Towards Closing the Performance Gap in Cross-Modal Place Recognition
items.description: Cross-modal place recognition (CMPR) matches natural language descriptions against databases of geo-tagged reference images, enabling localization without visual queries.
items.ai_summary: CrossPlace is a two-stage cross-modal place recognition framework that uses a visual backbone and a token-level cross-attention reranker to match natural language descriptions to reference images.

items.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
items.description: Agent patches are larger than developers', which is widely read as over-editing. But patch size does not say whether the extra edits are needed, what they are, or where they come from.
items.ai_summary: Delta Residue Attribution is a method that replays agent trajectories and replaces code units to measure and analyze unneeded edits in repository-level coding agent patches.

items.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
items.description: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones.
items.ai_summary: Shape-aware three-way merge operator for RDF knowledge graphs uses SHACL shapes to detect semantic conflicts and validate results without losing or fabricating triples.

items.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support.
items.ai_summary: Survey of large language models in telecommunications examines privacy, security, and ethical challenges, and outlines a telecom-specific taxonomy and open research directions.

items.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.description: Since vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, accelerating these demonstrations before fine-tuning can lead to faster VLA policies without an additional speed-selection module at deployment.
items.ai_summary: RePace is an offline reasoning framework that uses a pretrained language model to determine variable speedup profiles for human demonstrations, accelerating vision-language-action policies.

items.title: Focus Only on What's Important: Training-Free Focus Maps for Frozen Vision Transformers in Long-Video Object Segmentation
items.description: Vision transformers are strong but costly image encoders for video object segmentation. Training-free token merging cuts compute uniformly across the frame, including on tracked objects.
items.ai_summary: Training-free focus map policy for frozen vision transformers in long-video object segmentation protects targeted objects and reduces counted encoder compute while maintaining high accuracy.

items.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
items.description: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets.
items.ai_summary: BOP-Refer benchmark pairs monocular images from 9 BOP datasets with referring expressions and ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes to evaluate monocular 3D and 2D object grounding.

items.title: DocDUR-Net: Degradation-Aware Unified Document Image Restoration
items.description: Captured document images often suffer from diverse degradations caused by uncontrolled imaging conditions, which reduce readability and obscure fine text structures.
items.ai_summary: DocDUR-Net is a degradation-aware unified document image restoration network that uses a perception module and adaptive feature fusion to restore degraded document images without external task selection.

items.title: Model Weights, Airlocks and Sandboxes: A Call for Technical Validation of Re-identification Tests under the EDPB Anonymisation Guidelines
items.description: The Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), published for consultation in July 2026, assess anonymity relative to the entities that may access data.
items.ai_summary: Framework for validating re-identification tests under European Data Protection Board anonymisation guidelines examines measurement practices across model weights, airlocks, and regulatory sandboxes.

items.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
items.description: Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud.
items.ai_summary: Decision-focused fine-tuning method for autoregressive tabular transformers maximizes expected utility under cost matrices for cost-sensitive financial events.

items.title: TIDE-Flow: Fine-Grained Temporal Evidence and Structured Displacement Matching for Spike Optical Flow
items.description: Spike cameras capture high-speed motion through an integrate-and-fire mechanism, providing fine-grained temporal observations without exposure blur.
items.ai_summary: TIDE-Flow is a spike-based optical flow estimation framework that uses temporal integration evidence and displacement evidence encoding to model motion from spike camera binary streams.

items.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
items.description: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions.
items.ai_summary: DRBench Pro is a knowledge-centric benchmark using local knowledge trees and evidence-grounded rubrics to evaluate the breadth and depth of coverage in professional deep research agents.

items.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
items.description: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry.

items.title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series.
items.ai_summary: Diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts in large language models by evaluating performance under controlled temporal interventions.

items.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
items.description: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality.
items.ai_summary: ResNet-50 classifier that identifies the source of images generated by text-to-image models with high accuracy by detecting subtle visual idiosyncrasies.

items.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
items.description: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question.
items.ai_summary: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent is an algorithmic framework that iteratively optimizes knowledge base structures for large language models using question-answering discrepancies.

items.title: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk
items.description: We study risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in finite discounted infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes with recursive entropic risk measures (ERM), parameterized by $β\neq 0$. We consider both risk-averse ($β>0$) and risk-seeking ($β<0$) settings.
items.ai_summary: Model-based algorithm called ERM Value Iteration Lower Confidence Bound that establishes rigorous sample complexity guarantees for offline reinforcement learning under recursive entropic risk.

items.title: Diffusion Steering via Adaptive Reward Estimation and Resampling
items.description: Text-to-image diffusion models can generate images that satisfy complex prompts, yet often produce images that omit requested objects, attributes, or relationships.
items.ai_summary: TrailMix is a training-free method that adaptively guides text-to-image diffusion generation by redistributing probability toward parallel lookahead trajectories with higher reward scores.

items.title: datasette-charts 0.3a0
items.description: Release: datasette-charts 0.3a0 I added chart annotations to datasette-charts ! You can now render a chart and then annotate it with lines, shaded areas, labels, or a combination of the three.
items.ai_summary: Python package datasette-charts adds support for rendering chart annotations with lines, shaded areas, and labels.

items.title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
items.description: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs.
items.ai_summary: Computational framework using large language models to analyze thousands of English proverbs, quantifying their prescriptive power and recommendations across human judgment domains.

items.title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
items.description: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved.
items.ai_summary: Proximal Bregman response function framework that repairs trustworthiness failures in distilled language models while preserving downstream performance and avoiding the original transfer corpus.

items.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
items.description: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution.
items.ai_summary: Empirical study comparing how joint-embedding predictive architectures and recurrent state-space models shape epistemic uncertainty through their training objectives and architectures.

items.title: Beyond Feature Fusion: Sensor-Grounded Semantic-Spiking Learning for Robust Object Detection
items.description: Underexposure weakens object details, and overexposure obscures boundaries. Spike cameras encode light into high-frequency binary streams. Long-window spike counts give stable appearance cues, while short observations reveal changes in firing rates from sparse measurements.
items.ai_summary: SPIRE is a sensor-grounded semantic-spiking framework that uses high-frequency spike streams to achieve illumination-robust object detection under varying exposure conditions.

items.title: Gradient TD($λ$) for Non-Linear Function Approximation
items.description: Temporal difference (TD) learning is central to reinforcement learning. Many methods use semi-gradient TD, which may diverge, or develop algorithms with mean-squared Bellman or TD-error objectives that are difficult to analyze.
items.ai_summary: Gradient TD method extends temporal difference learning with the projected Bellman error objective to non-linear function approximation in reinforcement learning.

items.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
items.description: LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs.
items.ai_summary: RouteabilityBench and the Routeability Audit Protocol propose a retrospective audit package to evaluate prompt-specific variation and routeability in large language model portfolios.

items.title: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
items.description: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models.
items.ai_summary: Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark provides a largely automated pipeline and vetted question sets to evaluate large language models on early-grade literacy foundations across multiple languages.

items.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
items.description: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache).
items.ai_summary: LoopTitan demonstrates that parameter revisit in looped Mixture-of-Experts architectures yields negligible gains when compared against matched non-revisit controls.

items.title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
items.description: Emotionally supportive interactions require large language models not only to avoid overtly harmful content, but also to recognize vulnerability-related risk, regulate their relational stance, preserve user agency, and provide context-appropriate support.
items.ai_summary: VulnSafe is a Chinese capability assessment framework that measures vulnerability-aware relational safety and response competence across large language models.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss
items.description: Collecting data from wireless sensors can be challenging when limited communication infrastructure prevents them from offloading their measurements.
items.ai_summary: F-MADDPG is a flexible multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that enables decentralized data harvesting across variable sensor populations and permanent agent losses.

items.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
items.description: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights.
items.ai_summary: Cross-architecture initialization aligns a target network to the representational geometry of a guide network, transferring optimization priors and improving downstream performance.

items.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
items.description: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out?
items.ai_summary: Coding agents outperform generative video models on visual reasoning tasks by synthesizing programs that render answer videos from initial frames and prompts.

items.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
items.description: HOG-WAM improves visually robust control in world-action models by adding future Histograms of Oriented Gradients as auxiliary structural supervision through a training-only HOG diffusion transformer, yielding higher success under observation corruptions while preserving the…

items.title: WorldExpand: Building Coherent 3D Worlds via Sparse Joint Panoramic Expansion
items.description: Constructing complete 3D worlds from a single panorama is challenging because large portions of the scene remain unobserved.
items.ai_summary: WorldExpand builds coherent 3D worlds from a single panorama by jointly generating sparse, high-resolution panoramic observations using coverage-guided view selection and joint diffusion.

items.title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
items.description: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks.
items.ai_summary: Barron smoothness framework characterizes optimal discretization errors for deep neural networks using layer-wise generalizations of Barron norms and an equidistribution principle for local minima.

items.title: Guidance as Variance Matching
items.description: Guidance repels the prediction of a diffusion model away from a weaker reference prediction. It substantially improves sample quality, but its mechanism remains poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Variance-matched guidance is a closed-form rule for diffusion models that selects guidance scales by matching predicted variance to data variance, recovering hand-picked scales and improving sample quality without tuning.

items.title: Split-RL: Local Conflict Resolution in Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies are often trained by mixing contradictory feedback that is localized in space and time. For example, a robot may prioritize speed in open areas versus precision in tight gaps.
items.ai_summary: Split-RL is a gradient boosting trees reinforcement learning algorithm that isolates conflicting feedback objectives by routing updates into disjoint state-space regions to prevent signal interference.

items.title: CIRKDV2: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation with Contextual Modeling for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
items.description: Existing Knowledge Distillation (KD) methods for semantic segmentation often guide the student to mimic the teacher's structured information generated from an individual image. However, they ignore the global semantic relations across various images that are valuable for KD.
items.ai_summary: Cross-Image Relational KD V2 is a semantic segmentation knowledge distillation method that transfers structured pixel and channel relations modeled from global images to improve student feature representation.

items.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
items.description: Large language models increasingly replace real people in the AI development pipeline, as they are used to generate training dialogues at scale and to drive alignment and evaluation.
items.ai_summary: PersonaFactory is an end-to-end pipeline that generates detailed user personas and uses them to produce structured synthetic user prompts and multilingual conversations for training and evaluating large language models.

items.title: SceneDesigner3D: Agentic Evolutionary Search for Principled Rearrangement of 3D Indoor Scenes
items.description: Scene rearrangement is an essential task for 3D content creation applications, requiring generation of diverse, aesthetic and functional scene rearrangements.
items.ai_summary: SceneDesigner3D is an agentic evolutionary search method that uses vision-language models to systematically rearrange 3D indoor scenes based on aesthetic, physical, and functional design principles.

items.title: Generation as Reverse Encoding
items.description: Pretrained visual representations accelerate generative learning by abstracting away appearance and spatial detail. Yet the same abstraction makes the return to pixels far harder, shifting much of the burden onto a larger decoder.
items.ai_summary: RevFlow is a generative framework that uses intermediate representations of a frozen encoder as successive generative targets to accelerate both learning and sampling in diffusion models.

items.title: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumour Classification
items.description: Accurate and early classification of brain tumours from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for treatment planning, yet many published deep learning studies are trained and tested on small, single-source datasets, reporting accuracies that may not hold outside these…
items.ai_summary: A comparative study of deep learning architectures for brain tumour classification evaluates six models using a leakage-aware data pipeline to ensure robust cross-dataset generalization.

items.title: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets
items.description: In a Houston 2024 replay, replacing a fixed 20 percent battery reserve with a county-risk threshold raises observed five-hour backup coverage from 75.0 percent to 86.5 percent and adds USD 10.2 in modeled annualized margin per home (paired 95 percent interval: USD +1.7 to USD…
items.ai_summary: HomeFleet-ERCOT is a residential battery benchmark and controller suite that explores adaptive reliability reserves to improve backup coverage and economic margins during power outages.

items.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
items.description: SPLICE improves reinforcement learning on long-horizon agent tasks by constructing local training targets from failed trajectories using a proposal model to select splice points and generate bounded options, outperforming GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines.
items.ai_summary: SPLICE is a reinforcement learning method that constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories to improve agent performance on long-horizon tasks.

items.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
items.description: To avoid the quadratic cost of dense attention over long contexts, models such as DeepSeek-V4 and Hy4 have turned natively sparse, and speculative decoding, which matters most where decoding is slowest, increasingly runs on them.
items.ai_summary: DFly2 is a block-parallel speculative decoding drafter that shares the target model's KV cache and sparsity selections to eliminate the drafter's context cache and scoring pass.

items.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming the economics of intrusion by reducing the attacker's cost to scan and adapt, while tempting defenders into unbounded compute.
items.ai_summary: Stateful deception framework for cyber defense that uses adversary-specific persistent state and local language models to impose high computational costs on attackers while reducing defender resource expenditure.

items.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
items.description: Tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) work well across tabular classification problems but can fail silently at deployment when distributions shift.
items.ai_summary: CALD is an unsupervised monitor that detects harmful out-of-distribution shifts in tabular foundation models by finetuning the decoder to maximize disagreement with test predictions.

items.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
items.description: Two nodes with identical connections within their own layer can differ in importance if their neighbors in another layer occupy different positions in the network.
items.ai_summary: InterConRank is a joint node centrality algorithm that computes separate, interconnected rankings for each layer of a heterogeneous network to improve node importance evaluation.

items.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
items.description: LLM agents increasingly rely on external memory, yet they still hallucinate about what they remember. Often the correct memory is retrieved and placed in the prompt, but the answer contradicts it or the memory is applied to the wrong question.
items.ai_summary: TASK memory is a framework combining text notes, activation steering, and knowledge editing to eliminate memory-use hallucinations in large language model agents.

items.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
items.description: Preference-aligned LLMs can exhibit mode collapse, concentrating their output distributions around a narrow set of high-reward responses. This limits creative generation, which requires quality, novelty, and diversity.
items.ai_summary: SEPO is a training-free system prompt ensemble optimization framework that generates diverse, high-quality, and novel responses by evolving and selecting system prompts.

items.title: Reading Fine-Tuning Diffs Through Lenses: Model Diffing for Backdoor Detection
items.description: We introduce a common scoring system based on token readouts to evaluate weight, activation and output-based model diffing methods for backdoor detection in fine-tuning processes.
items.ai_summary: Scoring system using token readouts to evaluate model diffing methods for backdoor detection, showing that the J++-lens improves weight-based backdoor identification.

items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.description: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts.
items.ai_summary: CARE-OPD is an adaptive on-policy distillation method for long-horizon agents that expands history coverage and uses execution evidence to reduce training time and environment actions.

items.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
items.description: Mathematicians solve problems faster when they know the right theory. We ask how much a stated theory is worth to a large language model (LLM) solver, and whether a model can write that theory itself.
items.ai_summary: Method for measuring the value of mathematical theories to large language model solvers by evaluating how stated or self-induced theories improve problem-solving success and efficiency.

items.title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
items.description: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks.

items.title: BRIAR: Martingale Belief Smoothing on Bifurcation-Guided Reasoning Trees
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has rapidly advanced long-chain reasoning, yet standard policy optimizers distribute rollout compute and gradient credit blindly across a trajectory.
items.ai_summary: BRIAR is a tree-structured reinforcement learning framework that uses martingale belief smoothing to optimize reasoning traces and allocate rollout compute for language models.

items.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering?
items.description: Embodied QA needs memory, but answer accuracy mixes retained evidence, reading errors and question priors. For a simulated multi-room scene-graph pipeline we define answerability: the fraction of questions a fixed rule-based reader answers correctly from the graph alone.
items.ai_summary: Evaluative study on how vision-language scene graphs serve as memory for embodied question answering, demonstrating that graph memory improvements do not always increase answer accuracy.

items.title: Was the Model Given the Right Action? Auditing and Repairing Action Interfaces in Navigation World Models
items.description: World models are evaluated by predicting future observations from actions. These evaluations assume that actions are prepared the same way as during training, but an unchecked mismatch can make a model appear less accurate than it is.
items.ai_summary: ActRosetta is a tool that detects action encoding mismatches between training and rollout in navigation world models and repairs inputs to reduce visual prediction error.

items.title: From NP-Hardness to Exact Tractability Through Sample Abundance
items.description: Additional observations can make exact optimization tractable without changing the objective or feasible set.
items.ai_summary: Additional noisy observations can make noisy parity fitting and other worst-case NP-hard optimization problems exactly tractable with high probability using efficient algorithms.

items.title: WorldInteract: Controllable Streaming Video Generation for Multi-Material Interactions
items.description: Video world models aim to create interactive physical worlds that capture how diverse materials move and interact. Yet material-dependent dynamics remain underexplored in controllable video generation, limiting reliable control in scenes with different materials.
items.ai_summary: WorldInteract is a streaming video generation framework that models cross-material interactions by separating material behavior generation and contact response computation using physical rewards.

items.title: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks
items.description: The emerging field of weight space learning has demonstrated the potential to enable metanetworks, i.e. models that process neural network (NN) data, to support several steps of the machine learning lifecycle, from model optimisation to evaluation and adaptation.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks leverage input architecture hierarchies with permutation-symmetry-preserving pooling layers to scale weight space learning to large neural networks like ResNet-18 and Transformers.

items.title: Bigger Model or Bigger Table? How Much Backbone a Chorus N-gram Module Replaces
items.description: We ask how much of a transformer's backbone the Chorus N-gram module replaces. Chorus adds hashed tables of token bigrams and trigrams to its input and attention.
items.ai_summary: Chorus adds hashed token n-gram tables to transformer inputs and attention to replace portions of the model backbone while maintaining comparable loss and efficiency.

items.title: LiDAR Intensity Reconstruction with Limited Real Data: An Architecture Benchmark under Fixed-Epoch Training
items.description: Physics-derived simulation can supplement scarce real-world LiDAR intensity measurements, but its effectiveness depends on the learning architecture and the amount of real training data available.
items.ai_summary: A fixed-epoch training benchmark evaluates nine neural architectures for LiDAR intensity reconstruction, showing that UNet-V2 and diffusion models excel depending on the amount of real data.

items.title: Robust Recourse under Causal Graph Ambiguity
items.description: Causal algorithmic recourse recommends actions to reverse unfavorable decisions by modeling how interventions change an individual's features. Existing methods typically assume one causal graph that describes the system and account for uncertainty in the causal mechanisms.
items.ai_summary: Worst-Case Recourse and Graph-Weighted Recourse find low-cost algorithmic recourse actions that succeed across multiple plausible causal graphs by relaxing strict robustness constraints.

items.title: Privileged On-Policy Distillation for Calibrated Alzheimer's Diagnosis With Missing Modalities
items.description: Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed from clinical, biospecimen and imaging evidence, but few patients undergo every test. Because these modalities are complementary, a missing one has many plausible values.
items.ai_summary: Privileged On-Policy Distillation uses specialized teacher models to grade missing modality imputations during training, producing a well-calibrated Alzheimer's diagnosis model for any test combination.

items.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
items.description: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization.
items.ai_summary: ReMoT extracts transferable detection knowledge from frozen visual foundation models using staged joint attention across RGB and wavelet views to detect AI-generated images accurately.

items.title: Spec2Weights: Certifying Networks that a Language Model Writes from a Specification
items.description: A language model can write the weights of a small MLP, CNN, RNN or GNN from a plain-language specification, with no data and no gradient step. We ask when such a network can be proved exact in the float32 arithmetic it actually runs in.
items.ai_summary: Spec2Weights certifies neural networks generated by language models from plain-language specifications by proving exactness in float32 arithmetic using combinatorial checks and error bounds.

items.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
items.description: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories.
items.ai_summary: Two-stage reasoning framework called INSPIRE improves the forecasting of emerging entities in temporal knowledge graphs by combining shared patterns and individual evidence.

items.title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling
items.description: Data allocation methods often use a small proxy model to select training data for a larger target model. However, this proxy can rank data differently from the target, leading to suboptimal training performance.
items.ai_summary: Mismatch-corrected multi-fidelity bandits improve adaptive data selection for training large target models using smaller proxy models by accounting for ranking mismatches.

items.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) directly trains a unified policy across domains to continually expand agent capabilities without training separate specialists or requiring an extra distillation stage.
items.ai_summary: Mixed-task reinforcement learning approach called Maco-RL uses a quota-based scheduler and tri-buffer sampling to scale agent capabilities across multiple domains efficiently.

items.title: Effect of class proportion shifts on classifier curvature
items.description: Changing the class mix can alter mean loss without changing the classifier.
items.ai_summary: Class proportion shifts in ten-class classification are analyzed using loss Hessian traces, and initial class gradients successfully forecast how much the trace changes.

items.title: Seeing the Right Context: Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Remote Sensing
items.description: Remote sensing scene understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to interpret queried targets in relation to nearby objects and surrounding structures, which serve as spatial references or define the scope of an answer.
items.ai_summary: Grounded on-policy distillation method called GeOPD improves multimodal large language models for remote sensing by making contextual spatial relationships explicit during training.

items.title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
items.description: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models rarely satisfy all behavioral requirements of a new platform, and teams without a large deployed fleet lack the data to address the resulting failures. We propose a failure-driven data flywheel for post-training such models.
items.ai_summary: Failure-driven data flywheel framework automatically generates target driving scenarios and post-trains vision-language-action models to significantly reduce collision rates.

items.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
items.description: Interactive world models must generate video continuously while responding promptly to user actions. Real-time throughput alone leaves input latency unresolved: coarse generation blocks delay action updates, and generation after input adds work to the response path.
items.ai_summary: Fine-grained speculative streaming framework called ShowNow uses playback-time computation to prepare action-conditioned futures, drastically reducing input-to-display latency in interactive world models.

items.title: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding
items.description: Poetry-to-video generation requires more than translating text into visual scenes. Poetic language is highly compressed, often depends on historical and cultural knowledge, and frequently conveys meaning through metaphor, imagery, and other non-literal expressions.
items.ai_summary: Agentic framework and benchmark called PoVi translates compressed and metaphorical poetic language into grounded visual scenes through structured planning and video generation.

items.title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
items.description: High traffic demand during hurricane evacuations causes severe congestion on major highways, leading to delays and safety risks for evacuees. Predicting evacuation traffic in real-time can significantly enhance evacuation management efforts.
items.ai_summary: Generalized dynamic graph learning framework uses data from multiple historical hurricanes to predict evacuation traffic up to six hours in advance for unseen storms.

items.title: Technical Report MEG2text: Beyond Alignment in Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
items.description: Non-invasive brain-to-text seeks to recover language from brain activity without surgery. A central challenge is turning learned brain-language representations into accurate word predictions.
items.ai_summary: Decoding system called MEG2text recovers language from non-invasive brain activity by combining brain-text alignment, class-balanced word readouts, and language-model fusion.

items.title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
items.description: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it.
items.ai_summary: ClueRL proposes a reinforcement learning approach that helps vision-language models spot distinctive visual details to improve knowledge-based entity recognition.

items.title: Neural Rendering Compiler: Generative Video Models as Programmable Renderers
items.description: Generative video models are becoming powerful renderers, yet lack the predictable control interfaces of conventional systems such as HTML/CSS engines or Blender. Their capabilities emerge implicitly from training, making it difficult to determine what they can reliably execute.
items.ai_summary: Neural Rendering Compiler automatically probes frozen video models to construct capability manuals and compile user intent into model-specific execution strategies.

items.title: Provably Efficient Concave Utility Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation
items.description: Concave utility reinforcement learning (CURL) unifies a diverse range of problems, including standard reinforcement learning (RL), imitation learning, and maximum entropy exploration.
items.ai_summary: Model-based optimistic concave utility policy optimization efficiently estimates occupancy measures to solve concave utility reinforcement learning in finite-horizon episodic bilinear MDPs.

items.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
items.description: RoboEvo$^2$ recursively co-evolves a coding-agent harness and a vision-language-action policy, using policy failures to discover reusable skills and preference distillation to improve motor control, yielding large success gains without extra human demonstrations.

items.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
items.description: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision.

items.title: Learning to Be Truncated: Preparing LLM Checkpoints for SVD Compression
items.description: Compression based on singular value decomposition (SVD) often requires subsequent fine-tuning or weight correction to mitigate performance degradation. Budget-specific optimization must be repeated for different compression ratios.
items.ai_summary: LLift fine-tunes a low-rank approximation at a single ratio to prepare pretrained language models for singular value decomposition compression across multiple deployment budgets.

items.title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
items.description: In industrial prescriptive maintenance, an equipment supplier's model may recommend an intervention that a plant schedules, a contractor executes, and a quality or safety function approves.
items.ai_summary: Permissioned-blockchain endorsers use verified proofs of calculation to authorize industrial maintenance prescriptions and stop mis-operated work orders.

items.title: Counting Beyond Frames: Codec Motion Tells Frozen Diffusion VLMs How Many
items.description: Counting how many times something happens is among the simplest questions about a video and among the hardest for video-language models, autoregressive and diffusion alike.
items.ai_summary: CoDiCount turns video codec motion into testable count hypotheses to improve how frozen diffusion vision-language models count actions and repetitions.

items.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
items.description: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in sequential decision-making, but learning effective policies often requires substantial interaction experience.
items.ai_summary: Autonomous LLM-based coding agents synthesize control policies by reasoning directly over readable world models, matching conventional reinforcement learning with less experience.

items.title: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification
items.description: This paper introduces Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, designed for training and evaluating deep learning models for movement classification.
items.ai_summary: Atunda introduces a systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves and trains temporal convolutional neural networks to achieve over 95% classification accuracy.

items.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
items.description: Autonomous research agents are emerging as a promising approach to scientific problem-solving across disciplines, owing to their growing ability to improve a solution through repeated experiments.
items.ai_summary: REE introduces a benchmark of 100 open-ended scientific research problems to evaluate how autonomously AI agents iteratively improve starter solutions.

items.title: A Hard Background Pairing Transfers across Classifiers and Images
items.description: An image classifier names the object in an image, and its accuracy is the share of images named correctly. A classifier that names a car on a road may miss the same car pasted onto clouds.
items.ai_summary: Composite image benchmarks reveal that the hardest object-background pairings discovered for certain image classifiers remain difficult for held-out classifiers across new photographs.

items.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics
items.description: Many embodied world models predict future states in latent spaces optimized for RGB reconstruction, which do not explicitly prioritize object-level semantics and geometry relevant to motion generation.
items.ai_summary: MotionRep is a visual representation world model that jointly generates future DINO representations and 3D object flow to model object-centric dynamics for robotic manipulation.

items.title: Distractor-Robust Reinforcement Learning via Variational Bisimulation
items.description: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) promises data efficiency and generalization, but typical reconstruction-based objectives encourage models to waste representational capacity on task-irrelevant distractors.
items.ai_summary: VIBES is an adversarial model-based reinforcement learning objective that replaces pixel reconstruction to discard task-irrelevant distractors while retaining task-relevant information.

items.title: PRAM: Activating Latent Multimodal Knowledge through Partwise Reasoning
items.description: Emergent cross-modal classification and retrieval enable transfer between modalities without direct paired supervision. However, existing methods often prioritize sample-level alignment, overlooking local discriminative information and partwise statistical relations.
items.ai_summary: PRAM is a partwise reasoning framework that activates latent multimodal knowledge in frozen encoders by composing partwise statistical relations across modalities.

items.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
items.description: A vision encoder turns an image into one vector per patch, refined layer by layer. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) writes each vector of one layer as a sum of learned directions, most with a coefficient of zero.
items.ai_summary: Feature ablation analysis shows that removing a sparse autoencoder feature and its matched counterpart from another seed produces similar encoder output changes for up to 70% of pairs.

items.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
items.description: Large pretrained language models provide capable policies for interactive tasks, but how much model capacity is necessary for a specialized language agent? We introduce ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents (SLAs) from scratch.
items.ai_summary: ZeroHero is a framework that trains small language agents from scratch using expert demonstrations, proximal policy optimization, and reasoning alignment.

items.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits.
items.ai_summary: LatentRL-QAS is a latent space transfer framework for reinforcement learning-based quantum architecture search that maps quantum circuits of any qubit count into a shared latent space.

items.title: Predicting acute food crises and discovering actionable drivers with causal machine learning
items.description: Acute food insecurity is driven by a compound of conflict, adverse climate events, displacement, and economic shocks.
items.ai_summary: Causal machine learning pipelines incorporating driver variables forecast acute food crises and identify conflict as a primary causal driver of crisis classification.

items.title: DecisionReplay: A Corpus and Offline Simulator for Ensembling Decision Models
items.description: Comparing ensembles, routers and cascades requires the output of every model on every item, and its cost. Stored collections built for routing keep no per-option probabilities.
items.ai_summary: DecisionReplay is a dataset and simulator containing probability vectors, costs, and latencies from commercial decision models to facilitate offline ensembling and routing research.

items.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
items.description: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation.
items.ai_summary: HoMe is an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively optimizes memory system harnesses for AI assistants by identifying failure mechanisms and versioning memory sessions.

items.title: From Models to Services: Systematizing Security Assurance for Model-as-a-Service
items.description: Large language models are mainly delivered as cloud services, in which the assets of different principals are coupled within a single service pipeline, while the related security research is scattered across several fields with differing threat models.
items.ai_summary: A systematic security assurance study decomposes Model-as-a-Service into a five-layer stack, analyzes threat models and security goals across 120 studies, and evaluates 50 defenses.

items.title: Beyond Pose Control: Anatomically Consistent Ultrasound Video Generation
items.description: Camera-controlled video generation anticipates how a scene appears from new viewpoints by relying on a prior learned implicitly from large-scale data.
items.ai_summary: Anatomically consistent ultrasound video generator that combines an anatomical prior and a 3D latent memory to improve visual fidelity, pose following, and anatomical consistency across thyroid, kidney, and lumbar spine scans.

items.title: Automated Batch-Variable Selection for ComBat-Based Radiomic Harmonization
items.description: ComBat harmonizes multicentre radiomic features, but batch variables are usually chosen manually, without a standardized criterion across image acquisition parameters.
items.ai_summary: ParsiComBat is an automated batch-variable selection method for ComBat harmonization that ranks candidate acquisition parameters, balances batch-effect removal against feature preservation, and abstains when technical variation is negligible.

items.title: Conditional Independence Graph Learning from Dependent Data Via Time-Delay Embedding
items.description: We consider the problem of inferring the conditional independence graph (CIG) of a high-dimensional stationary multivariate Gaussian time series which could be short-range dependent (SRD) or long-range dependent (LRD).
items.ai_summary: Time-domain approach based on time-delay embedding that estimates conditional independence graphs for stationary multivariate Gaussian time series using a penalized negative pseudo log-likelihood function with convex or non-convex regularizations.

items.title: Commit2Drive: Perception-Grounded Language Decisions as Commitments for Trajectory Planning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
items.description: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models introduce language reasoning into end-to-end autonomous driving. They output a language decision together with a trajectory, which makes the planner more interpretable.
items.ai_summary: Commit2Drive is an end-to-end autonomous driving framework that enforces language decisions as consistency constraints on trajectory planning using perception-grounded maneuver commitments and consistency losses.

items.title: Do We Really Need an LLM for Weight-Space Programming? A Deterministic Forward-Only Paradigm and Its Capability Boundaries
items.description: Recent work on Weight-Space Programming uses LLMs to edit neural weights with forward passes only, conflating LLM scripting with the underlying algebra of forward-only editing.
items.ai_summary: Forward Weight-Space Programming is a deterministic pipeline combining probing, localization, stratified operators, automatic routing, and verification to edit neural weights through forward passes without requiring an LLM optimizer.

items.title: DuCo: Exploiting Dual Cross-Layer Consistency for Sparse Geometric Attention
items.description: Dense global attention is crucial for capturing cross-view geometry in visual geometry foundation models, yet its quadratic complexity limits efficient inference on long image sequences.
items.ai_summary: DuCo is a training-free sparse attention framework that exploits historical attention information and value clustering to achieve efficient geometric inference in visual geometry foundation models.

items.title: Blind spatially varying PSF estimation for fluorescence microscopy
