items.description: Trending on Hacker News from comentr.com. 162 points and 106 comments.
items.ai_summary: Google Gemini refused to output lyrics to a nursery rhyme, citing content restrictions.

items.title: Carry – Save every AI conversations as Markdown, in a folder you Own
items.description: Carry let's you automatically save your chats from Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Grok as Markdown in a local folder on you computer. You can easily search across all apps and handoff to other if needed with one click.
items.ai_summary: Carry is a desktop tool that automatically backs up your ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok chats as local Markdown files for easy searching and cross-platform continuation.

items.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from lesswrong.com. 201 points and 76 comments.
items.ai_summary: Two AI agents running on the same inference server can reliably communicate even when sandboxed from direct messaging.

items.title: PenGPT: A Generative Transformer for Handwriting and Sketches
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from greydanus.github.io. 223 points and 39 comments.
items.ai_summary: Small transformer model that writes handwriting and draws sketches from text prompts or symbol tokens.

items.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
items.description: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months. Here's the video of the talk.

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from openai.com. 252 points and 76 comments.
items.ai_summary: OpenAI introduces a family of models capable of designing new protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code without specialized biology models.

items.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
items.description: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities.
items.ai_summary: OmniAct is a cross-embodiment robot manipulation policy that conditions on a kinematic graph to produce embodiment-specific behavior across diverse physical structures.

items.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
items.description: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance.
items.ai_summary: PointX is a feed-forward model that predicts multi-view consistent 3D intrinsics per surface point by querying tokens across unposed images.

items.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
items.description: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video.
items.ai_summary: DiaCap is an audiovisual language model that jointly produces transcripts, timestamps, and speaker visual descriptions for dialogue captioning and diarization.

items.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
items.description: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data.
items.ai_summary: BioLoom is a biomedical vision-language model trained on a 52-million-pair dataset structured from scientific articles to improve multi-domain zero-shot classification.

items.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
items.description: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions.
items.ai_summary: CoT-Proxy is a distillation method that trains long-horizon student policies using teacher actions and reasoning summaries without requiring access to hidden teacher chains-of-thought.

items.title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
items.description: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable.
items.ai_summary: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis is a dialogue re-cinematography method that uses view-invariant speech audio and speaker-aware audio gating to generate synchronized multi-camera shots from a single video.

items.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
items.description: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated.
items.ai_summary: Lost on Campus is a benchmark evaluating the embodied spatial reasoning of vision-language models in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting.

items.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
items.description: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements.
items.ai_summary: ROAM-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating embodied active spatial intelligence in indoor environments under robot motion and collision constraints using evidence verification.

items.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
items.description: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control.
items.ai_summary: iWAM is an action-prediction method that conditions policies on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation using a bidirectional flow map to reduce inference cost in real-time control.

items.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
items.description: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces.
items.ai_summary: Physicl Scenes is a dataset of 6,499 artist-created 3D scenes with detailed geometry, physical materials, and semantic annotations to support visual and embodied learning research.

items.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation
items.description: Language models can generate LEGO$^\circledR$ assemblies from text, but their builds often contain parts that collide or attach to nothing. The usual approach of rejecting and resampling invalid placements discards decoded tokens without guaranteeing a valid build.
items.ai_summary: BriConstrain is a geometrically constrained decoding method that restricts a pretrained language model's next-token probabilities to generate valid brick assemblies without collisions.

items.title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit
items.description: Qwen3.5-0.8B rarely finishes reasoning in thinking mode: at a 4,096-token budget only 1 or 2 of 500 MATH-500 answers close their think block (two seeds), and accuracy is 15.4%.
items.ai_summary: A fine-tuning method using small gradient edits on specific layers stops small language models from looping and complements weight edits in large models to improve reasoning accuracy.

items.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
items.description: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement.
items.ai_summary: Beta-Data is an adversarial teleoperation dataset and midtraining approach that builds low-level behavioral coverage to improve robot policy execution and online adaptation.

items.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
items.description: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question.
items.ai_summary: SAG-Mem is a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and uses query-time lexical expansion to retrieve complementary facts.

items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation.
items.ai_summary: MetaFORGE is a meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes natural-language skill specifications using execution feedback to improve automated code generation for parallel computing.

items.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models
items.description: Real-world speech is often partially observable: audio may be missing or corrupted by noise and competing speakers, while the speaker's lips remain visible. Recovering speech requires combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred from context.
items.ai_summary: Read My Lips is a collaborative method combining a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model to reconstruct speech from partially observable audio-visual data.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.description: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization.
items.ai_summary: Draft calibration for speculative decoding applies standard temperature scaling to the draft distribution to mitigate distribution mismatch and improve acceptance length by up to 10 percent.

items.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
items.description: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock.
items.ai_summary: Temporal conditioning introduces a time-aware transformer for chess behavioral cloning that encodes player clock states to improve move-quality predictions and performance under time pressure.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
items.description: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning maximum likelihood updates on archived model rollouts can recover the performance of online reinforcement learning without discarding computed knowledge.

items.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
items.description: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments.
items.ai_summary: GREMLIN generates random neural environments for meta-learning reinforcement learning rules to supply useful experience and improve agent learning.

items.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
items.description: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty.
items.ai_summary: Delegent is a multi-agent harness that delegates easy subtasks to small language models to reduce the inference cost of frontier models without sacrificing performance.

items.title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos
items.description: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research.
items.ai_summary: EventDiffusion is a hierarchical generative framework that directly learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real video recordings.

items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.description: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong.
items.ai_summary: AIChipBench evaluates LLM coding agents on automated AI accelerator design, showing that state-specific debugging feedback improves hardware synthesis success.

items.title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
items.description: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also…
items.ai_summary: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living dataset provides over eight hours of annotated radar recordings across five locations to support privacy-preserving activity recognition research.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.description: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth.
items.ai_summary: Uncertainty-aware entity linking preserves upstream ambiguity signals from named entity recognition using Monte Carlo dropout and fuzzy entropy to improve retrieval recall in cyber threat intelligence.

items.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
items.description: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference.
items.ai_summary: Shifter Quantization reconstructs native-width integer operands using shifted shared bits to improve low-bit LLM quantization quality and accelerate inference throughput.

items.title: FOL-Proof: Verifying LLM Text-to-Logic Translations via Deterministic Semantics
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate natural-language statements into first-order logic (FOL) to improve reasoning. However, LLMs are prone to errors, and so a semantically unfaithful FOL formula could corrupt downstream reasoning.
items.ai_summary: FOL-Proof is a semantic firewall pipeline that validates LLM-generated first-order logic translations against independent linguistic interpretations to improve reasoning accuracy.

items.title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys
items.description: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys.
items.ai_summary: An approach for generating object-centric event logs from patient journeys is presented to help investigate care delivery and health system design using process mining techniques.

items.title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers
items.description: Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise.
items.ai_summary: A theoretical study on error-correcting output coding with noisy binary classifiers derives upper and lower bounds for the excess error rate to determine the reliability function.

items.title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
items.description: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated evaluators in evaluation and training pipelines, their judgements are often affected by systematic biases that conflict with human preferences.
items.ai_summary: HUB-J is an integrated framework that uses human-LLM disagreement and agreement cases to automatically detect, quantify, and mitigate systematic biases in LLM judges.

items.title: U-Statistics-Powered LLM Reasoning
items.description: Since its introduction by DeepSeek, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted for training large reasoning models and agents, spurring a proliferation of its variants.
items.ai_summary: A pessimistic ratio estimator addresses the challenge of adaptive group size selection in group relative policy optimization, reducing mean squared error and improving policy training.

items.title: Understanding Clipping In Zeroth-Order Optimization
items.description: Zeroth-order optimization has emerged as a resource-efficient alternative to Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) when fine-tuning LLMs, thanks to the inherent low dimensionality of the loss landscape.
items.ai_summary: A systematic analysis of per-sample clipping in zeroth-order optimization reveals that it improves test accuracy and robustness by down-weighting hard-to-fit training examples.

items.title: SUPRA: Synthesizing Amyloid PET from MRI and Plasma Biomarkers with an Explicit Regional SUVR Prior
items.description: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) quantifies brain amyloid-$β$ as a standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), but is costly and not widely available.
items.ai_summary: SUPRA is a method for synthesizing brain amyloid PET images from structural MRI and plasma biomarkers by combining an explicit regional SUVR prior with a 3D network.

items.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
items.description: Voice activity detection (VAD) is one of the first steps in speech processing pipelines, from transcription and diarization to speech language models. Supervised detectors need labelled data and inherit the domain and annotation conventions of their training corpora.
items.ai_summary: ClusterVAD is an unsupervised voice activity detection method built on frozen speech foundation models that clusters representations to perform threshold-free detection.

items.title: Local Indices Are Not Enough: Synchrony and Global Information in Bandit Algorithms
items.description: Standard index-based stochastic bandit algorithms such as KL-UCB and Thompson Sampling achieve optimal $O(\log T)$ regret over a horizon $T$.
items.ai_summary: An investigation into bandit algorithms proves that asynchronous local index algorithms cannot achieve logarithmic regret, demonstrating that global information and synchrony are essential for optimality.

items.title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement
items.description: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once.
items.ai_summary: Empirical analyses show that streaming chatbot answers progressively increases user preference votes compared to displaying complete stored answers instantly.

items.title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
items.description: Recent work proposes hypernetworks that convert a document into a low-rank parameter update (LoRA) in a single forward pass, enabling fast injection of new knowledge into a frozen LLM.
items.ai_summary: Latent-space LoRA merging method combines hypernetwork-generated LoRAs in the intermediate latent space, improving performance over weight-space and factor-space baselines while maintaining a single fixed-rank adapter.

items.title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes
items.description: Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods.
items.ai_summary: Theorem and Lean 4 machine-checked proofs establish that the product decoder of Error-Correcting Output Codes is MAP-consistent if and only if the code is a union of n-vs-Rest codes.

items.title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics
items.description: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) record the full spectrum of light at every pixel, so projecting an HSI through a camera's spectral sensitivities gives that camera's RAW image, and one HSI can supply training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline methods.
items.ai_summary: Spectrify framework converts 3D scene datasets into hyperspectral images using physically based optical models and a material-labeled reflectance spectra library to improve training data for low-level computer vision.

items.title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators
items.description: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity.
items.ai_summary: LiSM framework uses linear probes in the semantic mean-space of vision foundation models to provide training-free, lightweight control for representation-space generative models across global and local tasks.

items.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring.
items.ai_summary: Fixed-ranking benchmark evaluates eight heterogeneous uncertainty quantification signals for LLM-based recommenders, showing that ranking-aligned Top10Mass provides strong scalar Error@10 detection.

items.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
items.description: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles.
items.ai_summary: Technique-agnostic taxonomy organizes AI-native radio access network control around four functional capabilities to evaluate hybrid AI systems, decision-making processes, and reproducible simulation platforms.

items.title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements
items.description: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise.
items.ai_summary: SHARPnP framework combines joint registration and plug-and-play fusion for reference-free, RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy and unaligned camera measurements.

items.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
items.description: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference.
items.ai_summary: Method using Claude LLMs edits raw network weights as text to perform tool-free 4-bit quantization repair, recovering most of the accuracy lost during standard round-to-nearest quantization.

items.title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment.
items.ai_summary: SALSA generative framework samples adversarial suffixes from learned distributions to enable fast and efficient LLM safety vulnerability assessments and black-box jailbreak attacks.

items.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
items.description: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP).
items.ai_summary: Score-based generative model operates in the t-spectral domain of hypergraph signal processing to generate and denoise signals on fixed hypergraphs and recover missing nodes.

items.title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution
items.description: We study best arm identification (BAI) with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting. After choosing an action, the learner observes a post-action context together with a reward whose distribution depends only on this context.
items.ai_summary: A Track-and-Stop algorithm optimizes best arm identification with unknown post-action context distributions by matching an instance-dependent sample complexity lower bound.

items.title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors
items.description: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$.
items.ai_summary: PAC-type probabilistic lower bounds quantify the input-conditional coverage of conformal predictors without requiring assumptions on the underlying data distribution.

items.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
items.description: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations.
items.ai_summary: RecordRoute couples comparative localization with local diagnosis to audit agent execution failures by ranking records through trajectory comparisons.

items.title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
items.description: GRAPE-Bench jointly evaluates video reasoning under visual degradation and question difficulty, exposing model weaknesses and enabling improvement and control.
items.ai_summary: GRAPE-Bench jointly evaluates video reasoning models across various visual degradation conditions and question difficulties using synthetic and real-world footage.

items.title: E-MAPS: Event-Based Promptable Video Segmentation with Memory-as-Prompt
items.description: RGB-based video object segmentation (VOS) remains brittle under fast motion and adverse illumination. Event cameras preserve signal under blur and challenging exposure, but provide little evidence when motion slows.
items.ai_summary: E-MAPS transfers a pretrained promptable segmenter to event streams using Event-to-Token alignment and Memory-Aware Prompting for video object segmentation.

items.title: RePix-VFI: Re-rendering Observed Pixels for Video Frame Interpolation with Generative Priors from One-Step Diffusion
items.description: Multi-frame video frame interpolation (VFI) aims to reconstruct dense video from sparse keyframes, requiring accurate intermediate motion and faithful appearance.
items.ai_summary: RePix-VFI is a multi-frame video frame interpolation framework that couples draft-conditioned one-step video diffusion with the re-rendering of observed keyframe pixels.

items.title: Training Lightweight Gaze Models without Target Gaze Annotation: What Makes a Good Teacher?
items.description: Model-generated labels offer a scalable route to training lightweight vision models, but what makes a model a good teacher, and can we tell before training a student?
items.ai_summary: Model-generated labels from specific teachers can train lightweight gaze target estimation models that match the accuracy of models trained on human annotations.

items.title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
items.description: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition.
items.ai_summary: RFW-W provides a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable assets to task-conditioned scene composition for embodied simulation.

items.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
items.description: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions.
items.ai_summary: Access to clinical evidence and full trajectory information significantly improves the reliability of large language model judges in detecting unsafe clinical actions.

items.title: MESSI: Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration for Physics-Based Character Control
items.description: Physics-based soccer characters must perform diverse motor skills and transition smoothly between them, such as dribbling into a shot.
items.ai_summary: MESSI uses shared adaptation and a context-conditioned low-rank adapter to enable smooth physics-based character transitions between multiple soccer skills.

items.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
items.description: A new benchmark shows that many robot manipulation policies perform worse when mirrors are present, often because they confuse reflections with real objects rather than simply colliding with the mirror.

items.title: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models
items.description: Visual token compaction reduces inference cost by passing only selected image patches or video tokens to later layers. In sequence models with local convolutions, each removal changes which tokens are neighbors.
items.ai_summary: ProbConv is a differentiable operator for state space models that computes expected convolutions under token compaction, improving performance as more tokens are removed across image, vision-language, and video tasks.

items.title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
items.description: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on external memory to retain and reuse information across interactions. Existing memory systems treat memory as a record of the past and evaluate it by fidelity to the conversation.
items.ai_summary: Leto is a utility-centric memory system for large language model agents that uses an index and a response-based utility loop to anticipate and supply required future context.

items.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
items.description: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear.
items.ai_summary: LEGOSpec is a composable framework for speculative draft design that isolates component effects and introduces DFlux, a balanced draft model that improves acceptance length across various workloads.

items.title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation
items.description: Recent advances in deep learning and the public availability of computed tomography (CT) datasets with paired reports have enabled many Text-to-CT generators. However, their evaluations almost always differ in preprocessing and metrics, which hinders comparison.
items.ai_summary: CtrlCT is an evaluation toolkit that tests the credibility and anatomical control of text-to-CT generators by analyzing how report edits systematically change generated computed tomography scans.

items.title: First-Hit Photoconsistency for Neural Surface Reconstruction
items.description: Recent neural implicit and Gaussian splatting approaches have achieved impressive results in multi-view surface reconstruction. However, jointly optimizing geometry and appearance introduces ambiguities.
items.ai_summary: A neural surface reconstruction method uses multi-view patch photoconsistency with geometry-based visibility and sphere tracing to achieve accurate geometry without volumetric rendering or parametric appearance models.

items.title: Modelling Billingual Learning Through LLM Training: A Critical-Period Exploration
items.description: Critical-period accounts of second-language (L2) acquisition suggest that the ability to learn a new language may depend on how easily previously acquired first-language (L1) knowledge can be modified.
items.ai_summary: An exploratory computational study uses small language models to examine second-language acquisition, finding that elastic weight consolidation slightly reduces parameter drift during sequential training.

items.title: PAVE: Preference-Aligned Visual Egocentric Learning for the Blind and Low-Vision Users
items.description: Egocentric video question answering enables blind and low-vision (BLV) users to query their immediate surroundings through natural language.
items.ai_summary: PAVE is a visual egocentric learning framework for blind and low-vision users that combines structured answer-policy fine-tuning, query routing, and filter-GRPO alignment to improve assistive response quality.

items.title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration
items.description: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates.
items.ai_summary: Radev is a decision-native 3D medical multimodal model that combines anatomy-guided visual compression, single-pass candidate prediction, and counterfactual calibration to improve clinical decision-making from CT scans.

items.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
items.description: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it?
items.ai_summary: A study on foundation models proposes the potentiality principle, showing that task adaptation can be achieved largely through a constant, input-independent shift vector per layer.

items.title: AVQ-Attention-2: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention with Exact Local Blocks and Linear-Cost Training
items.description: Attention costs $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ in the number of tokens.
items.ai_summary: AVQ-Attention-2 is an adaptive vector-quantized attention mechanism that uses exact local blocks and cluster means to achieve linear-cost training and efficient inference without requiring fine-tuning.

items.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
items.description: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps.
items.ai_summary: CAPER is a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that uses vision-language models to generate reliable assembly procedures with improved inventory consistency and part reliability.

items.title: When Repair Accuracy Misleads: Training a VLM on Its Own Failures
items.description: Fine-tuning a vision-language model on its own failures is a direct way to repair it, but accuracy on held-out failures, the obvious measure of success, misleads.
items.ai_summary: Verified failure-driven repair fine-tunes vision-language models on verified failure cases to improve spatial reasoning accuracy while revealing vulnerabilities in negation tasks.

items.title: NEST: Uncovering and Nesting Unknown Objects in Open-World Object Detection
items.description: Open-world object detectors aim to localize objects of classes not covered by their training annotations, but most label them only as "unknown".
items.ai_summary: NEST is an open-world object detector that uses a class-agnostic ranker and taxonomic reasoning to uncover and categorize unknown objects.

items.title: File Size as a Potential Dataset Bias in Audio-Visual Deepfake Data
items.description: Deepfake detection benchmarks are commonly designed to evaluate whether models can distinguish authentic from manipulated audiovisual content. However, benchmark construction pipelines may introduce unintended associations between class labels and simple file-level properties.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of audio-visual deepfake datasets reveals that simple file-level properties like file size and duration can create significant dataset biases.

items.title: Teaching Time Without Losing General Retrieval: Adapting Multimodal Embeddings for Time-Sensitive Video Retrieval
items.description: In text-to-video retrieval, MLLM-based embedding models do well when the text describes the scene (general retrieval), but poorly when it describes actions and their direction (time-sensitive retrieval).
items.ai_summary: TARA-inspired techniques adapt multimodal embedding models for time-sensitive video retrieval by combining keeping loss, pair loss, and middle-layer LoRA training.

items.title: FocusAnchor: Zero-Shot Metric Depth by Anchoring a Depth Foundation Prior to Focus Cues
items.description: Existing depth-from-focus methods can struggle with weak focus cues, new cameras, or fewer focal slices.
items.ai_summary: FocusAnchor is a recurrent model that uses focus-volume lookups and a depth foundation prior to achieve zero-shot metric depth estimation across varied cameras.

items.title: Eliciting the Recall Capacity of Linear Attention
items.description: Linear attention models exhibit a disproportionate deficit relative to softmax attention in associative recall (AR) in language modeling. We investigate this gap through natural language evaluations, synthetic recall tasks, and targeted training interventions.
items.ai_summary: Targeted training interventions such as sentence repetition and loss reweighting elicit the underutilized associative recall capacity of linear attention models.

items.title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans
items.description: People can anticipate how an object moves and the effort an interaction may require by watching others. How can embodied agents acquire this understanding from video?
items.ai_summary: VidForce is an approach that estimates interaction trajectories and force profiles from third-person RGB videos using learned physical prototypes as priors.

items.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
items.description: Reliable driving VLMs must do more than answer correctly or localize relevant scene actors: they must determine whether the available visual evidence is sufficient to support an answer.
items.ai_summary: DriveAnswer is a benchmark of over 20,000 questions designed to evaluate whether vision-language models can determine if visual evidence is sufficient for autonomous driving tasks.

items.title: Polynomial-Time Learning of Random Automata from One Label per Word
items.description: We study a binary deterministic finite automaton whose $2n$ transitions are chosen independently and uniformly from its $n$ states. The learner observes independent uniform words of length $m$, each labeled with a single bit indicating acceptance.
items.ai_summary: A polynomial-time algorithm learns random binary deterministic finite automata from single-bit word labels by comparing label moments at consecutive history lengths.

items.title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents
items.description: AI agents are beginning to automate data analysis, orchestration, and simulation steering in HPC environments, but they introduce a security problem that existing cluster defenses do not address: the hijacked authorized agent.
items.ai_summary: A runtime defense system called AEGIS uses behavioral attestation and system-call interception to detect compromised AI agents in high-performance computing environments and trigger cluster-level containment.

items.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
items.description: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor.
items.ai_summary: A benchmark study demonstrates that off-the-shelf large language models can successfully automate advance-fee scam conversations to extract payments from users.

items.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
items.description: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes.
items.ai_summary: A lossless KV cache compression method called LoomKV accelerates large language model serving and reduces memory usage by storing compressed key-value states in GPU memory and SSD tiers.

items.title: FedTumor-IoMT: Federated Learning-Aided Brain Tumor Diagnosis on Resource-Constrained Edge IoMT Devices
items.description: Joint brain tumor segmentation and classification models are computationally intensive, limiting their training on resource-constrained edge platforms and restricting privacy-preserving Federated Learning FL in the Internet of Medical Things IoMT.
items.ai_summary: A multitask federated learning framework enables privacy-preserving brain tumor segmentation and classification on resource-constrained edge devices using selective encoder freezing.

items.title: OmniHarness-RSI: Modality-Aware Harness Evolution for Omnimodal Understanding
items.description: Recent advances in harness-based recursive self-improvement (RSI) have improved video understanding by evolving executable agent workflows without updating foundation model parameters.
items.ai_summary: A modality-aware framework called OmniHarness-RSI improves omnimodal understanding by factorizing agent evolution into specific perception and collaboration dimensions and recursively refining agent harnesses.

items.title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning
items.description: Systematic conservation planning must allocate limited protection budgets sequentially under ecological and climatic uncertainty.
items.ai_summary: A reinforcement learning framework combines proximal policy optimization with an implicit quantile network to improve systematic conservation planning under ecological and climatic uncertainty.

items.title: Online V-Learning with Adaptive Longitudinal Data
items.description: Reinforcement learning methods for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes are increasingly applied in mobile health (mHealth), where treatment decisions are made continually. Luckett et al.
items.ai_summary: A statistical theory establishes the consistency and asymptotic normality of online V-learning for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes from adaptively collected longitudinal data.

items.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
items.description: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use.
items.ai_summary: A benchmark of 100 day-to-day tasks called ShellBench shows that model choice has a greater impact on AI agent performance than agent harness selection.

items.title: PHM-ensemble: Scalable and Stable Probabilistic Multiresolution Clustering via Ensemble Density Estimation
items.description: Clustering is a foundational tool for exploratory data analysis across the sciences.
items.ai_summary: A probabilistic framework called PHM-ensemble performs multiresolution clustering by pooling mixture models from an ensemble of fits to deliver scalable, stable, and interpretable exploratory data analysis.

items.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
items.description: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible.
items.ai_summary: A benchmark analysis of quantum kernels on breast data finds that reported quantum advantages often stem from comparator selection, data leakage, or evaluation choices rather than inherent quantum superiority.

items.title: ProX-MAD: Aggregating Spatial Context into Representative Proxies for Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection
items.description: Few-shot medical anomaly detection (MAD) has largely followed a dataset-specific "one-for-one" paradigm, leaving unified "one-for-many" modeling underexplored.
items.ai_summary: ProX-MAD is a proxy-based framework that aggregates spatial context into compact, learnable proxies for unified few-shot medical anomaly detection across diverse datasets.

items.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
items.description: Metacognition includes knowing one's own strengths and weaknesses across kinds of tasks, not only judging whether a single answer is correct.
items.ai_summary: An evaluation of vision-language models reveals that they struggle to predict their own visual weaknesses in advance, though response probabilities can signal these errors during generation.

items.title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens
items.description: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited.
items.ai_summary: A study on conversational AI interaction styles shows that supportive chatbots consistently improve user satisfaction and trust across different cultural contexts.

items.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
items.description: Lembas treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget, using an iterative water-filling algorithm and attention reuse to improve long-video and multi-turn understanding with fewer tokens and less compute.
items.ai_summary: Lembas is a token allocation framework for video retrieval-augmented generation that optimizes frame and subtitle token budgets to improve long-video understanding efficiency and accuracy.

items.title: HARI4D: Hand-Articulation Aware 4D Reconstruction of Human-Object Interaction
items.description: Reasoning about human-object interaction from RGB cameras is important for gaming, VR environments, and robot learning. Yet 4D reconstruction from a monocular RGB camera is challenging, especially when articulated hands are involved.
items.ai_summary: HARI4D is a hand-articulation-aware method for reconstructing spatially and temporally consistent 4D human-object interactions from monocular RGB video.

items.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
items.description: A developer checking an assistant's report may need only an alarm that a claim is unsupported. A generative verifier, however, can continue decoding to quote and classify the errors. We study how much of that output is needed to recover its decision.
items.ai_summary: A generative verification method stops text decoding early to efficiently check assistant reports for unsupported claims without requiring full error localization generation.

items.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
items.description: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result.
items.ai_summary: A theory-informed quantum error mitigation method uses Fourier neural operators to recover correct order estimates from noisy circuit measurements in Shor order finding.

items.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
items.description: InstructReplay preserves an instruction-tuned language model's general abilities during fact fine-tuning by keeping its responses close to the initial model's answers on general instructions, reducing benchmark decline while still learning new facts.
items.ai_summary: InstructReplay is a fine-tuning method that preserves a language model's general abilities by having it replay its own initial answers to general instructions during training.

items.title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search
items.description: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance.
items.ai_summary: SOARS is a training-free framework that uses a fast relevance estimation model to improve answer accuracy and reduce latency in deep search agents.

items.title: IMPACT-Seg: Consistent Anatomical Segmentation and Representation Learning Across CT, CBCT, and MRI
items.description: Computed tomography (CT), cone-beam CT (CBCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide complementary representations of the same underlying anatomy, yet substantial differences in image appearance challenge consistent segmentation and deformable registration in adaptive…
items.ai_summary: IMPACT-Seg is an anatomical segmentation framework that uses shared network parameters to maintain consistent segmentation and representation learning across CT, CBCT, and MRI images.

items.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
items.description: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging.
items.ai_summary: Motion-Conditioned World Modeling incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions to improve embodied visual tracking performance and cross-environment generalization.

items.title: Label leakage through file headers: geometry and batch confounds in public mammography datasets, and a pre-training acceptance gate
items.description: A dataset whose diagnostic label can be recovered from non-diagnostic information yields high, reproducible and uninformative model performance.
items.ai_summary: Pre-training controls applied to public mammography datasets reveal that non-diagnostic information like image geometry and file headers can yield uninformatively high diagnostic performance.

items.title: DualSpec: Spectral Reconstruction with Optimized Stereo Cameras
items.description: Spectral imaging captures information that ordinary RGB sensors cannot, but dedicated spectral cameras can be expensive and bulky.
items.ai_summary: DualSpec is a stereo acquisition framework that jointly optimizes two external optical filters and a reconstruction network to recover dense spectra from RGB images with reduced error.

items.title: Shared information governs multi-view planted matching
items.description: We study when the rows of $K$ shuffled views of the same $n$ objects can be matched, where each object is observed once in every view through a Gaussian feature vector with known covariance.
items.ai_summary: Theoretical analysis reveals the exact shared information and bipartition thresholds that govern when shuffled views of identical objects can be successfully matched across multiple views.

items.title: Biomechanically Grounded Prediction of Selective Motor Control and Clinical Outcomes from Infant Video
items.description: Early identification of cerebral palsy (CP) relies on observational assessments of spontaneous infant movement, such as the General Movement Assessment (GMA) and the Baby Observational Selective Control AppRaisal (BabyOSCAR), which require trained raters and substantial scoring…
items.ai_summary: Baby Biomechanical 3D Body is an infant-adapted pipeline that estimates joint-angle trajectories from single-camera video to predict clinical outcomes like selective motor control and cerebral palsy.

items.title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations
items.description: Online hate speech is an ever-growing issue with negative impacts on both groups and individuals, potentially causing users to withdraw from online conversations and debate.
items.ai_summary: Multilingual large language models fine-tuned on a new annotated dataset successfully detect constructive speech, hate speech, and agreement in online social media comments.

items.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
items.description: A reinforcement learning method rewards agents for delaying commitment until their inferred posterior over answers is sufficiently narrow, improving evidence-based answering across vision-language benchmarks.

items.title: 3D Tracking Any Point with Events and Frames
items.description: Tracking a fast-moving point in 3D is prohibitive when RGB frames are blurred or too far apart to reveal its motion. Event cameras record brightness changes between frames, providing measurements inside these temporal gaps.
items.ai_summary: TrackAnyMotion combines monocular RGB frames and event camera data to track arbitrary points in 2D and 3D, significantly reducing endpoint errors even during rapid motion or frame gaps.

items.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
items.description: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand.
items.ai_summary: An adaptive digital twin framework based on in-context learning with large language models predicts electromagnetic transients in data centers for unseen configurations without model retraining.

items.title: Simultaneously Boosting Efficiency and Capability for Linear Attention via Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification
items.description: Self-attention's quadratic complexity constitutes a core bottleneck for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
items.ai_summary: ACCAP-LA embeds an adaptive channel compression and activation purification mechanism into linear attention to reduce computational complexity while boosting Vision Transformer accuracy and cross-architecture compatibility.

items.title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
items.description: Recovering the continuous world-space motion of both hands from egocentric video is essential for applications such as human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality.
items.ai_summary: MemHand uses short-term event and long-term scale memories to reconstruct continuous world-space hand motion from egocentric videos, maintaining high accuracy through severe occlusions and out-of-sight intervals.

items.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
items.description: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization.
items.ai_summary: Researchers evaluate six large language models across three microscaling formats and introduce Midmax, a calibration-free scale-selection strategy that improves accuracy in MXFP4 configurations.

items.title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
items.description: Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce UDV-Rebalance, a Transformer reparameterization method that uses an auxiliary diagonal matrix to maintain unit-norm columns and rows, yielding a tuning-free rule that remains effective across model scales and architectures.

items.title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
items.description: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins.
items.ai_summary: Researchers measure numeric leakage across linked LLM prompts and find that fresh scaling keys allow attackers to recover confidential prices and profit margins significantly more often than reused maps.

items.title: CityRecast: Suppressing Persistent Artifacts in Generative Satellite 3D Reconstruction
items.description: Satellite-based 3D reconstruction is limited by sparse observations and changes across acquisition dates. Existing methods use generative priors to recover missing visual detail, but ghosting, streaking, and blur persist in their Gaussian scenes.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce CityRecast, a generative satellite 3D reconstruction method that suppresses persistent artifacts in low-elevation renderings through Gaussian scene repair and observation calibration.

items.title: Tabra Blends: Improving the Accuracy--Latency Trade-off with Complementary Tabular Models
items.description: Tabular foundation models make different trade-offs between prediction accuracy and latency. We study whether a compact ensemble can deliver higher accuracy in less time.
items.ai_summary: Researchers show that blending a compact ensemble of Kumo and LimiX models achieves higher prediction accuracy and lower latency than individual tabular foundation models across TabArena splits.

items.title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions
items.description: Discrete skill policies execute motions drawn from a finite vocabulary. In most current methods, this vocabulary is a latent codebook learned jointly with a selector and a decoder.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce Movement Prototype Quantization, a method that places a library of demonstrated motions after a trained policy to evaluate skill vocabularies without training additional parameters.

items.title: Speculative Decoding for Semantic-ID-Based Generative Recommendations
items.description: Generative recommender systems with Semantic IDs (SIDs) represent each item as a short sequence of $L$ discrete tokens and use a sequence model to predict the next item's tokens from a user's history.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose SIDECAR, a speculative decoding method for generative recommenders that uses approximate draft candidates and tree-attention passes to certify exact top-K items efficiently.

items.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
items.description: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce PathGrad, a gradient estimator that differentiates Langevin path probabilities to fine-tune machine learning force fields against experimental measurements without unstable trajectory gradients.

items.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
items.description: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument.
items.ai_summary: Researchers analyze measurement artifacts in trustworthiness evaluations of quantized small language models and release item-level predictions, option scores, and human annotations to improve compression assessments.

items.title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited
items.description: We present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects through Perspective-n-Point.
items.ai_summary: Researchers present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects in real time.

items.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields
items.description: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by the interaction dynamics of Particle Life. In Particle Life, each particle has a colour, and an interaction matrix sets how strongly each colour attracts or repels each other colour.
items.ai_summary: Cellular automaton called Field Life models the interaction dynamics of Particle Life using chemical fields to simulate moving structures and patterns.

items.title: Aqua2CAD : Observation-Guided Point Cloud Correction and Completion for CAD Reconstruction from Underwater Stereo Images
items.description: Recovering editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from underwater stereo images requires accurate and complete geometry, yet stereo reconstruction produces displaced points and missing regions.
items.ai_summary: Aqua2CAD is a two-stage method that uses view-conditioned correction and a shape prior to recover accurate CAD models from underwater stereo images.

items.title: PtychoFM: A Foundation Model for Ptychographic Imaging
items.description: Ptychography provides high-resolution lensless imaging across X-ray, electron, and optical microscopy, but reconstructing images from diffraction measurements generally requires computationally intensity iterative phase retrieval.
items.ai_summary: PtychoFM is a physics-aware foundation model that reconstructs complex object images directly from individual ptychographic diffraction patterns at high speeds.

items.title: SAVERA: Bridging Frozen Vision and Language Models via Sparse Alignment and Visual Evidence Reuse
items.description: Independently pretrained vision and language models may learn shared structures of the same underlying world, providing a foundation for combining them to build multimodal capabilities.
items.ai_summary: SAVERA is a multimodal framework that combines frozen vision and language models using sparse alignment and prompt-guided residual fusion.

items.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
items.description: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response.
items.ai_summary: EEG-World is a recurrent world model that forecasts human brain EEG band-power dynamics using audiovisual stimuli and preceding EEG data.

items.title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
items.description: Artificial intelligence systems for computed tomography (CT) remain largely restricted to specific anatomical regions, examination types or predefined abnormalities, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive and spatially grounded interpretations.
items.ai_summary: FORA is a general-purpose CT model that recognizes radiological concepts, localizes abnormalities, and generates reports across multiple scan protocols.

items.title: PhysMend: Verification-Guided Program Refinement for Physics-Aware Video Generation
items.description: Video generative models synthesize realistic scenes, yet their interactions often violate physics. A ball dropped onto sand should displace grains and settle into a crater, whereas a generated video may show it passing through the surface or leaving the sand flat.
items.ai_summary: PhysMend is a training-free framework that refines physical programs for video generation by verifying events on simulated rollouts and depth controls.

items.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
items.description: Residual Guidance is a training-free method that counteracts context inertia in streaming video generation by adding a residual from denoising the previous chunk under the new prompt to early denoising steps, improving prompt switching without training or per-model tuning.

items.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow
items.description: Viscoelastic flow past two side-by-side microcylinders has been shown to exhibit geometry-dependent transitions among symmetric, converging, diverging, and asymmetric-diverging flow states, together with regions of bistability and tristability.
items.ai_summary: Data-driven framework learns a parameter-dependent normal form to model geometry-dependent flow transitions and bistability in viscoelastic fluids from sparse measurements.

items.title: Beyond Image-Text Pairs: Aligning Semantic Changes for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
items.description: Image-text alignment serves as a foundation for modern vision-language models (VLMs), yet prevailing training paradigms provide limited supervision for learning how semantic changes correspond across modalities.
items.ai_summary: Post-training method aligns cross-modal semantic changes using controlled visual and textual variations to improve fine-grained visual understanding in vision-language models.

items.title: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
items.description: SpatialArena is an open benchmark that evaluates geometric models across five 3D perception tasks using uniform metrics and robust alignment, revealing that single-image depth is near saturation on public benchmarks but progress now depends on cross-frame and cross-view…
items.ai_summary: SpatialArena is an open benchmarking platform that evaluates and compares geometric foundation models across multiple tasks and diverse datasets.

items.title: E(n)-Equivariant Spherical Decision Surfaces
items.description: We present a constructive derivation of exactly E(n)-equivariant spherical decision surfaces by extending prior O(n)-equivariant hypersphere neurons to include translations.
items.ai_summary: Method that derives exactly E(n)-equivariant spherical decision surfaces without input centring or explicit pairwise differences to improve geometric primitive modeling.

items.title: Breaking the Joint Action Space Dependence in Distributionally Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.description: We study the sample complexity of learning robust coarse correlated equilibria (CCE) in finite-horizon, general-sum, distributionally robust Markov games with known rewards and a generative model of the nominal transitions.
items.ai_summary: Algorithm that reduces sample complexity in distributionally robust multi-agent reinforcement learning by depending on the largest individual action-set size rather than joint action space.

items.title: Interactive Neural Computers
items.description: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability.
items.ai_summary: Interactive Neural Computer uses a generative desktop model with a surprise-gated slot memory to recall off-screen content and assist with operating system tasks.

items.title: EPRO: Robust Policy Optimization Through an Imperfect Execution-Policy Predictor
items.description: RL for LLMs often separates rollout generation from policy training. Although the two numerical engines share model parameters, they can induce different policies.
items.ai_summary: Execution-Policy Robust Optimization uses a differentiable predictor and shift-aware soft clipping to improve reinforcement learning stability and performance for large language models.

items.title: From Grammar Deltas to Token Masks: Incremental Constrained Decoding under Runtime Grammar Evolution
items.description: Grammar-constrained decoding enables large language models to generate outputs that satisfy formal constraints, but in code and domain-specific language generation, the relevant constraints are not always fully available before decoding and may emerge progressively from new…
items.ai_summary: GramDelta is an incremental constrained decoding framework that propagates runtime grammar updates without replaying historical prefixes or recompiling caches.

items.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
items.description: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed.
items.ai_summary: MRScissors is a team-selection method that separates task requirements from measured physical capabilities to identify minimal feasible teams in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation.

items.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
items.description: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence.
items.ai_summary: Language models pre-trained with sleep mechanisms use recurrent forward passes to improve in-context learning speed and reduce out-of-distribution next-token prediction loss.

items.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
items.description: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates.
items.ai_summary: Study that establishes power-law scaling relationships for ensemble uncertainty, model capacity, and diversity in large language models to improve epistemic uncertainty estimation.

items.title: Is Prosody Encoded in the Neural Audio Codec Mimi?
items.description: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become a fundamental infrastructure for modern speech-language models, discretizing continuous speech signals into token sequences that enable large language models to process and generate audio.

items.title: Back to Raw Motion: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers for Text-to-Motion and Exact Conditional Generation
items.description: As generative models tackle larger and more complex datasets, learned codecs enable efficient generation through compact latent representations, but may lose details and cannot guarantee exact preservation of given conditions.
items.ai_summary: RawMo is a latent-free diffusion transformer framework that generates and refines motion directly in raw motion space for text-to-motion and conditional tasks.

items.title: Accuracy of Noise Ceiling Estimators for Brain Scores
items.description: The internal activations of modern machine learning models align surprisingly well with the activities recorded in real brains. In the last five years, the alignment between encoding models and brain activities, often called brain scores, has steadily increased.
items.ai_summary: Unified mathematical framework that derives closed-form expressions for four noise ceiling estimators, revealing that existing methods underestimate the true noise ceiling in different settings.

items.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
items.description: SimPWM uses a parameter-free simulator as a proxy to generate robot videos and simulated states, revealing that video models follow arm motion more reliably than object dynamics and often ignore simulated object state.
items.ai_summary: SimPWM is a simulator-as-proxy world model that represents robots and objects in 3D to render realistic videos and simulate states for robot manipulation tasks.

items.title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
items.description: Large language models exhibit a middle-heavy intrinsic-dimensionality profile in their feed-forward layers, and using this profile to guide width allocation improves pruning under a fixed parameter budget.
items.ai_summary: Method that uses principal component analysis to measure layer-wise intrinsic dimensionality in feed-forward networks, improving width allocation and performance in large language models.

items.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
items.description: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization.
items.ai_summary: NABLA is a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for stochastic optimization that automatically adjusts its second-moment memory using a closed-loop feedback rule.

items.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
items.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems.
items.ai_summary: C3H is an inference-time attack for multimodal recommender systems that exploits compression-to-consensus bias to promote target items while maintaining recommendation utility.

items.title: Beyond Fixed-Context Likelihood: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Text Detection via Context Perturbation Discrepancy
items.description: The same increase in token log probability from earlier context can be typical at one position and unusually large at another.
items.ai_summary: Context Perturbation Discrepancy is a zero-shot AI-generated text detector that measures token log probability gains relative to a pretrained language model expectation.

items.title: Beyond Static Semantics: Instance-Adaptive Vision-Language Alignment for Building Damage Assessment
items.description: Instance-level building damage assessment (IBDA) from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery remains challenging, as the same damage grade may exhibit diverse visual manifestations across individual buildings.
items.ai_summary: LAMIA-IBDA is a vision-language framework that uses adaptive text-visual alignment and dynamic instance-prototype grounding for instance-level building damage assessment from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery.

items.title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
items.description: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve.
items.ai_summary: Contrastive Identification of Actions is a learning method that improves latent world models by identifying executed actions among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal.

items.title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop
items.description: Database agents need more than schema structure: business meanings, stored values and reference queries supply knowledge that becomes relevant at different points in reasoning.
items.ai_summary: RubikSQL-HB is an agentic text-to-sql framework that provides database-specific knowledge workspaces to help agents interleave knowledge access with SQL construction and execution.

items.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
items.description: In Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, semantic tools such as mineBlock pick targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility test, so a buried ore the agent has never seen is one call away, and scores cannot show whether the agent searched.
items.ai_summary: EviCraft is a runtime and benchmark that enforces evidence closure in Minecraft agents by restricting their decisions to facts supported by direct observations or actions.

items.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
